Package frc.robot.util

Class OnboardLogger

java.lang.Object
frc.robot.util.OnboardLogger
public class OnboardLogger extends Object
Subsystem-scoped logger that writes structured data directly to the WPILib DataLog binary file (.wpilog) every loop cycle.

How to use

  1. Create one instance per logical subsystem, passing a namespace string: 
      OnboardLogger log = new OnboardLogger("Shooter");
  2. Register the values to log via the register*() methods. Each registration stores a supplier and a log-file entry â€” no file I/O happens at registration time.
  3. Call logAll() once per loop cycle (e.g., from robotPeriodic()) to evaluate all suppliers and write their current values to the log. If logAll() is never called, no data is ever written.

Namespace

The name passed to the constructor becomes a prefix for every registered key. For example, new OnboardLogger("Shooter") with registerDouble("Velocity", â€¦) creates the log path Shooter/Velocity. In AdvantageScope this appears as a folder named Shooter containing a signal named Velocity.

Self-registration

Each constructor call adds the new instance to the static loggers list so that logAll() can iterate over all instances without the caller keeping a reference. This is intentional: subsystem IO classes can create their loggers in constructors without wiring anything up in robotPeriodic().

      public OnboardLogger(String name)
      Creates a new logger for the subsystem identified by name and registers it with the global log-all list so logAll() picks it up automatically.
      Parameters:
      name - Subsystem namespace prefix (e.g., "Shooter", "Aiming"). All keys registered on this logger will appear under this path in the log file.

    • registerMeasurement

      public <T extends edu.wpi.first.units.Unit> void registerMeasurement(String name, Supplier<edu.wpi.first.units.Measure<T>> supplier, T unit)
      Registers a WPILib Measure (typed unit value) as a double in the specified unit.

      The unit name is stored as the log entry's metadata so AdvantageScope can display the correct unit label. If the supplier returns null at log time, a DriverStation.reportError(java.lang.String, boolean) is posted (visible in the DS console) and 0 is written to avoid corrupting the log stream.

      Type Parameters:
      T - The unit type.
      Parameters:
      name - Signal name.
      supplier - Supplier for the typed measurement; must not normally return null.
      unit - The unit to convert into when writing (e.g., Amps, Celsius).

    • logAll

      public static void logAll()
      Evaluates every registered supplier across all OnboardLogger instances and writes the current values to the .wpilog file.

      This method must be called once per loop cycle â€” typically from Robot.robotPeriodic() â€” or no data will ever be written to the log, regardless of how many signals have been registered. The WPILib DataLogManager handles the actual file I/O on a background thread, so this call is non-blocking.
